text:
alex: Heads-up — Kibana is returning sparse results for GPU-node ingest logs since ~08:10 UTC. Our SLO dashboards look OK but we can’t correlate request->trace for a subset of warmup/healthcheck traffic. Anyone seeing trace IDs dropped in the pipeline?

maria: seeing lots of short-lived connections from the warmup queue, high ingestion rate spikes. Could be relabel/sampling kicking in. :thinking_face:

jordan: I noticed a relabel rule we rolled last week that strips request_id for low-severity logs. Might be too aggressive for the new warmup pattern.

alex: @jordan can you paste the rule? If it matches a label like job=promtail and message =~ "warmup" that would do it.

jordan: rule is: `- action: replace
  source_labels: [severity, message]
  regex: "(debug|info);.*(health|warmup).*"
  target_label: request_id
  replacement: "-"`

maria: that replacement turns request_id into `-` which Loki treats as missing label. That explains missing correlation in Kibana (we rely on request_id label in Loki->ES enrichment).

devops: I ran a quick Loki query to show the gap and cardinality blowup:
```
{job="promtail", cluster="gpu-prod"} |= "warmup" | json | __error__!="" | count_over_time({job="promtail", cluster="gpu-prod"}[5m])
```
The spike at 08:11 is ~3x baseline. Indexing backpressure plus relabeling -> lost labels.

ingest-bot: Ingest metrics: promtail_ingest_rate=128k/s (08:11) vs baseline 42k/s; loki_write_errors=0.1% spike; relabel_drops=11k in that window.

sre-bot: Alerts fired: `LokiHighCardinality(critical)` (08:12), `KibanaQueryLatency(warn)` (08:14). Both silenced now but worth root cause.

alex: Ok, immediate plan: 1) revert the aggressive relabel replacement to keep request_id, 2) add a sampling exemption for cluster=gpu-prod, 3) tune Kibana query UI to increase result window while we backfill. Can someone own revert?

jordan: I’ll push a hotfix to remove the replacement and instead `target_label: dropped_request_id` so we preserve original `request_id`. Pushing in 2m.

maria: I’ll add a prom alert filter so that `promtail_relabel_drops{cluster="gpu-prod"}` triggers earlier; current alert threshold was too permissive.

devops: For troubleshooting, here's a quick curl against promtail status: `curl -s http://promtail-gpu:9090/metrics | grep relabel` — will paste outputs in thread.

alex: Good. Also we should check cost implications: that spike added ~10M extra ingested logs -> estimate $120 extra index cost for the day. Add to incident doc.

sre-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-GPU-INGEST. Assigned to eng-sre.

maria: After revert we should run this Loki query to verify request_id presence for warmup traffic:
```
{cluster="gpu-prod", message=~".*warmup.*"} |= "request_id" | json | label_values(request_id)
```

alex: Thanks all. After Jordan’s fix, wait 10m then run the label_values query + Kibana correlation to confirm traces reconnect. If not, we’ll roll a small customer-impact postmortem. :thumbsup:

jordan: fix merged @ 08:19 UTC. Rolling restart promtail-gpu in parallel.

ingest-bot: promtail relabel_drops decreased to 120 in next 10m window.

alex: Closing the loop: Kibana trace join shows request_id back for 98% of warmup logs. We still have ~2% gap — follow-up to investigate late-arriving logs and batching.

maria: opened follow-up ticket: TKT-743-fleet-ingest-sampling-exemption, assigning infra team to validate relabel rules across regions.

alex: Nice work. Leaving post-incident notes in INC-2026.
